summary:
Several well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces appeared on a website with 13 million monthly visitors. The videos include Dutch artists, TV presenters, Olympic athletes, former ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. The newspaper AD did not name the platform to protect victims. Outgoing justice minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to report them. Some managers and spokespeople confirmed that reports have been filed or legal steps are being considered.

Deepfake pornography is illegal under Dutch revenge porn laws. Victims can report to police, after which prosecutors may try to shut down the site, or they can start a mass claim, complain to the data protection authority, or contact hosting companies. A lawyer warned that more fake videos will appear if the government does nothing. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma was a victim, and a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a 180-hour suspended community service sentence last November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
